newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF to punish Nomura, DKB on Wednesday - papers.
newsitem.headline: MOF to punish Nomura, DKB on Wednesday - papers.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) is likely to announce administrative penalties on Wednesday against Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), both tainted in a high-profile payoff scandal, a business daily said on Tuesday.
The ministry is expected to suspend Nomura from stock trading for its own account by its equity department for four to five months, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
Nomura's corporate department will also be suspended from business for at least for four months, it said.
The daily Asahi Shimbun said the penalties against Nomura would come into effect early next week and would remain in place for four to six months.
Asahi also said MOF would order Nomura to submit a plan to improve its operations.
Nihon Keizai said MOF would probably bar DKB from extending new loans and might also limit bond trading for its own account.
The ministry is also likely to demand that DKB submit a plan to improve its operations, Nihon Keizai said.
Asahi said the penalties against DKB would remain in effect for four to six months.
